problems: The 2x lower bound holds only for the memory state in which the cited profile was taken (coherency 0.77 s, 18.7% of the call). The per-pair callbacks are stable in absolute time (about 2.8 s in both profiles). The memory-bound coherency is not: today it took about 5.3 s per call. With that composition the Amdahl ceiling, 1.48x, is below the row's 2x lower bound.

Under memory pressure (as with about 8 concurrent window workers in production) spectral_csm-shared-csm becomes the larger gd avenue, about 2.5x. spectral_psi_gd-1 becomes the smaller one. The stacking order and the credit split between the two gd rows would then flip.

On the ranking basis itself (summary.json family-warm 3.50-3.97 s per band, at the same scale as the 4.12 s profiled call), the figure is consistent with the Amdahl bound. The lower bound assumes the vectorised code costs at most 17% of today's band, about 0.6 s. That is untested.

The profiled composition comes from synthetic data where gd's output is all-NaN at 118x1024 and 32x1024 (summary.json result_statuses). Every pair's mask is empty, so linregress runs on fully masked input. EEG data with significant clusters may change the per-pair cost.

The risk class follows from the code fact given: a closed-form masked OLS reorders linregress's sums, so within-tolerance is plausible. The NaN pattern from min_group_size=3 must be kept. A future diff at 118x1024 would compare only NaN masks, because the output there is all-NaN.

The basis understates EEG cost: 10 EEG bands, each paying its own build, against 3 configured non-EEG bands. Composition on narrow EEG bands is similar to the full band (callbacks 31-33% in today's profiles).
The on-disk CSV is stale; the fresh build agrees on this row (rank 11, rank_basis_s 6635.77, after 3317.89).
